latest_release.body:
Fixes [#477](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/issues/477), [#478](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/issues/478) and [#469](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/issues/469): an app capturing the microphone or system audio no longer stops the bar from collapsing ([#475](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/pull/475)).

## v1.13.0

Four ways to reach and control your icons, all opt-in: with every default left alone, 1.13.0 behaves exactly like 1.12.0. None needs a new permission: they use the Accessibility permission hiding already asks for, plus the pointer and scroll monitors hover-to-expand already uses. They never read your screen.

### Added
- **Reveal without aiming** (off by default; Settings › General › "Also show hidden icons when you"). Show the hidden icons without hitting the small arrow: "Scroll down on the menu bar" (scroll up hides them again), "Click empty space in the menu bar" and "Shake the pointer at the top of the screen". Clicking anywhere off the menu bar hides what a gesture showed. Scroll and shake also work in the App Store build; the empty-click row is direct build only, because it needs Accessibility to tell empty space from an icon ([#493](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/pull/493)).
- **Find a hidden icon** (off until you record a shortcut; Settings › General › "Find a hidden icon"; direct build on macOS 27). The shortcut opens a search under the arrow that lists your running hidden apps. Type a few letters of a name or bundle id, then press Return to open that app's own menu without expanding the bar; the app hides again when the menu closes. Command-Return moves the app to visible, Option-Return to always hidden. Once a shortcut is set, the arrow's right-click menu also offers "Find a Hidden Icon..." ([#505](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/pull/505)).
- **Ask about new menu bar apps** (default Show It, which is the 1.12 behavior; Settings › Icons › "When an app adds a new icon": Ask Me, Show It or Hide It; direct build on macOS 27, only with Pinned sections on). With Ask Me, a new app stays visible, the arrow gets a dot, and clicking the arrow asks once, from a popover, whether to show it, hide it or always hide it. Hidden Bar remembers the answer, also after a restart. Apps still waiting for an answer sit first in the Icons list with a NEW tag, and an unanswered question lapses after 24 hours ([#503](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/pull/503)).
- **Presentation mode** (off by default; Settings › General › "Presentation mode"; direct build on macOS 27). While it is on, every third-party app icon is hidden (macOS's own items stay), and the apps you list as "Sensitive apps" stay hidden even if you click the arrow. Start it with your own shortcut (Settings › General › Presentation mode › "Keyboard shortcut") or the arrow's right-click menu, "Start Presentation Mode". A "Presenting" capsule shows how many apps are hidden and stops it; it names no app, since the screen may be shared. The first time it starts, a short tip under the capsule says what is hidden and how to stop it, once, and Settings has a "How it works" note. "Turn on automatically" starts it when a display is mirrored. It follows the "Show all icons when the microphone or camera turns on" switch: with the switch on, a microphone or camera that turns on while presenting pauses hiding once, so macOS can show the capsule that names the app using it, and nothing is hidden meanwhile, sensitive apps included; "Hide again" or any collapse resumes, and hiding resumes by itself when capture ends. With the switch off it never pauses, and a capture already on when presenting starts does not pause it. Reveal gestures and the new-app question wait while presenting, and the find-a-hidden-icon search leaves your sensitive apps out of its list ([#504](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/pull/504), [#509](https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden/pull/509)).

detail.readme:
## Hidden Bar Hidden Bar lets you hide menu bar items to give your Mac a cleaner look.

## 🚀 Install > **Official downloads.** Console Labs publishes Hidden Bar only through [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/consolelabs/hidden/releases), the Homebrew cask `hiddenbar`, and the [Mac App Store listing](https://itunes.apple.com/app/hidden-bar/id1452453066). Any other site offering Hidden Bar (for example `hiddenbar.app`) is not run by Console Labs. ###  App Store [![AppStore](img/appstore.svg)](https://itunes.apple.com/app/hidden-bar/id1452453066) The App Store build is sandboxed and cannot hide icons on macOS 27. On macOS 27, use the GitHub or Homebrew build below. ### Others The Hidden Bar is notarized before distributed out side App Store. It's safe to use 👍 #### Using Homebrew ``` brew install --cask hiddenbar ``` #### Manual download - [Download latest version](https://github.com/consolelabs/hidden/releases/latest) - Open and drag the app to the Applications folder. - Launch Hidden and drag the icon in your menu bar (hold CMD) to the right so it is between some other icons. ## 🕹 Usage * `⌘` + drag to move the Hidden icons around in the menu bar. * Click the Arrow icon to hide menu bar items, and click it again to show them. * Option-click the Arrow to reach the always-hidden section, a second group that stays hidden when you click the arrow. * Settings has the hide delay, a global shortcut, other ways to reveal icons (hover, scroll, shake) and the arrow style.

## 📚 Documentation - [Manual](docs/MANUAL.md): every setting, the hidden Terminal-only options, and troubleshooting. - [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): how the hiding trick works, topology, and known limits. - [Maintainer runbook](docs/RUNBOOK.md): build, behavioral verification, and release process. ## ✨Contributors This project exists thanks to all the people who contribute. Thank you guys so much 👏 [![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/0)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/0)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/1)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/1)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/2)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/2)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/3)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/3)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/4)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/4)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/5)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/5)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/6)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/6)[![](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/images/7)](https://sourcerer.io/fame/phucledien/consolelabs/hidden/links/7) Please read [this](CONTRIBUTING.md) before you make a contribution. ## Requirements macOS version >= 13.0 (Ventura) Running an older macOS? The last release supporting macOS 10.13 High Sierra through 12 Monterey is [v1.10](https://github.com/consolelabs/hidden/releases/tag/v1.10). Later versions require macOS 13 because autostart moved to the `SMAppService` API introduced there. ## You may also like - [Blurred](https://apps.apple.com/app/id1497527363) - A macOS utility that helps reduce distraction by dimming your inactive noise - [VimMotion](https://github.com/consolelabs/VimMotionApp) Vim style shortcut for MacOS ## License MIT © [Console Labs](https://console.so)
